caption: Figure 10.2: Near-to-far-field transformation (Near2FarMonitor) with PEC ground-plane image theory. Left: a 5-face Huygens box above an infinite PEC ground plane (ground_plane='−z') records equivalent tangential surface currents J_s = n̂ × H and M_s = −n̂ × E; exact image theory accounts for the lower face via image currents. Right: vector radiation integrals map the surface currents to the upper half-space (θ ∈ [0, π/2], φ ∈ [0, 2π]).
visual_intent:
Textbook-quality scientific schematic for a computational electromagnetics user manual. Flat vector style on a white background, high contrast, thin dark outlines, generous whitespace, sans-serif labels. Colour code used in every figure: primary grid G, total-field or forward-wave quantities in blue; dual grid G-tilde, scattered-field, backward-wave, or equivalent-current quantities in orange; exact/topological/reference items in dark grey; matched monitor surfaces and conserved-power items in green; truncation limits or unresolved features in red. Colourblind-safe. Every label must be spelled exactly as listed in this brief; mathematical symbols must be typeset correctly (hats, tildes, subscripts, transposes). Do not add any number, value, equation, software name, product name, logo, watermark or title that is not listed in this brief. Prefer fewer, larger labels over many small ones. No 3D photorealism, no cartoon characters, no hand-drawn or xkcd style.

Two panels side by side. LEFT PANEL (55% width): Cross-section of an antenna driven by 'port1' sitting above a horizontal dark-grey hatched plane labelled 'infinite PEC ground plane (ground_plane = "-z")'. Enclosing the antenna on the top and four vertical sides (5-face box, lower box face on the PEC ground plane) is the green 'Near2FarMonitor' box with outward normal arrows 'n̂', blue tangential magnetic surface current arrows 'M_s = −n̂ × E', and orange tangential electric surface current arrows 'J_s = n̂ × H'. Below the PEC ground plane, draw the dashed mirror-image 5-face box in light orange/blue labelled 'exact image theory: image currents'. RIGHT PANEL (45% width): Connected from the left panel by a thick grey arrow labelled 'vector radiation integrals (Balanis 2016)'. Draw a 3D upper half-space hemisphere dome above the ground plane with polar angle arc 'theta in [0, pi/2]', azimuthal angle arc 'phi in [0, 2*pi]', and a 3D radiation lobe inside the upper half-space. On the hemisphere surface mark orthogonal far-field unit vectors with labels 'get_farfield(TH, PH): Etheta, Ephi, Htheta, Hphi', 'directivity(TH, PH)', 'radiated_power()', and 'ludwig3(ff["Etheta"], ff["Ephi"], PH, reference="x"): co, cross'.
